fit_reason: The dominant leading-edge foundry and, through its CoWoS-type packaging, the single supplier of both leading-edge wafers and advanced packaging that nearly every AI accelerator needs. Both are central to its business, and it is the bottleneck the sub-sector is built around.

The world's largest outsourced packager and tester (OSAT), offering flip-chip BGA, fan-out wafer-level packaging, 2.5D interposers and 3D/stacked-die packages. Packaging is its core business, and it is the main outside alternative to TSMC for advanced packaging capacity.

A leading US-listed OSAT doing wafer bumping, flip-chip, wafer-level fan-out and system-in-package work. Advanced packaging is central to the business, and it is one of the outside packagers expected to absorb overflow from TSMC.

The sole supplier of EUV lithography systems, which every leading-edge wafer requires, plus metrology and inspection. Leading-edge wafer volume maps directly to its demand, and lithography is nearly the whole business.

The largest semiconductor wafer fabrication equipment maker, covering deposition, etch and related process tools used in every leading-edge fab. Wafer fab equipment is the whole business, so more wafer capacity means more demand.

A top supplier of etch and deposition (CVD, ALD) and wafer cleaning tools, including through-silicon via etch used in advanced packaging and memory stacking. Wafer fab equipment is central to the business, and it is a major beneficiary of capacity additions.

The leader in wafer and reticle inspection and metrology, also serving advanced packaging inspection. Process control is central to the business and demand rises with leading-edge complexity and fab capacity.

Integrated chipmaker whose Intel Foundry segment is the main US alternative to TSMC for leading-edge wafers and advanced packaging. Foundry is one of three segments and still ramping, so it is a meaningful rather than central part of the business, but it is the most prominent emerging alternative.

Maker of thermocompression bonding (TCB), flip-chip and wafer-level bonding equipment for advanced packaging, selling to OSATs and chipmakers. Assembly equipment is central, but it also has large exposure to mature wire-bonding markets.
Supplies inspection, 2D/3D metrology and packaging lithography tools with strong exposure to advanced packaging. Process control for wafers and packaging is central to the business.

Specialist in inspection and metrology for advanced packaging (Eagle-AP, fan-out panel inspection) and HBM-related interconnect packaging. Advanced packaging inspection is central, which makes it a direct play on packaging capacity growth.

The leader in dicing saws, grinders and polishers used to thin and separate wafers, which are critical steps in advanced packaging and HBM stacking. Wafer grinding and dicing is central to its business.

Supplies ultra-pure chemicals, filtration and wafer-handling products used throughout leading-edge fabs. Materials and contamination control are central, and demand tracks wafer starts and node complexity.
Provides optical and X-ray metrology for process control in leading-edge logic, foundry and advanced packaging. Metrology is the whole business, and its demand rises with leading-edge complexity.

Maker of EUV mask blank and photomask inspection systems, plus wafer and bump inspection. Inspection tools for leading-edge lithography are central, and it is a sole-source style supplier in EUV mask inspection.

A leading independent photomask maker supplying masks for integrated circuits and flat panel displays. Photomasks are required for every wafer pattern, and the product is the whole business, though its mix includes mature nodes and displays.
A major pure-play foundry, but focused on mature and specialty nodes rather than leading-edge, so it is a smaller alternative for AI wafers. Wafer foundry is the whole business.
A large wafer foundry focused on mature and specialty nodes rather than leading edge. Foundry is the whole business, but its exposure to AI accelerator wafers is limited.
An independent specialty foundry for analog, RF, silicon-photonics-adjacent and power processes. Foundry work is the whole business, but at specialty nodes rather than leading-edge logic.
Maker of single-wafer wet cleaning and electroplating equipment, selling heavily into China. Wafer cleaning equipment is the whole business, so it benefits from added wafer capacity.

Supplies deposition, ion-beam, wet processing and packaging lithography tools, including for advanced packaging and photonics. Semiconductor process equipment is the business, but its mix is broad and not focused on leading-edge logic.

Supplier of automated semiconductor test systems for wafer and packaged-device testing, with a growing AI compute test business. Test is a meaningful part of the business, alongside robotics and other segments.

Dominant maker of SoC and memory chip test systems and handlers, serving foundries and test houses. Test volume follows accelerator and HBM volume, so it is a meaningful part of the business, but test is downstream of wafers and packaging.
Maker of probe cards and wafer probing systems used to test chips at wafer level, including DRAM and HBM-related testing. Wafer-level test is a meaningful part of the business.
Provides test handlers, wafer-level and package test equipment and contactors. Back-end test is a meaningful part of the business, with less direct tie to leading-edge capacity.
Maker of wafer-level burn-in and test systems for logic, memory and photonics. Wafer-level reliability test is the business, but it is a small company with concentrated customers.
Maker of ion implantation equipment for chip fabrication, with a large mix in power and mature markets. Fab equipment is central, but its exposure to leading-edge AI wafers is limited.

Supplies vacuum, plasma power, gas delivery and metrology subsystems used in semiconductor process tools, plus laser systems for packaging and PCB. The semiconductor equipment share is substantial but not the whole business.
Maker of plasma power supplies and control systems used in wafer processing equipment such as etch and deposition. Semiconductor tool power is a large but not exclusive part of the business.
Builds gas and fluid delivery subsystems and precision parts for semiconductor equipment makers. Sub-supplier to wafer fab equipment, so volume exposure is indirect.
Builds gas and chemical delivery subsystems for semiconductor capital equipment makers. Sub-supplier whose volume follows wafer fab equipment demand.
Electronic materials and solutions provider for semiconductor chip manufacturing, spun out of DuPont. The description is thin, but its materials appear central to chipmaking and advanced packaging.

Diversified materials company with an electronics segment supplying semiconductor and advanced packaging materials, dielectrics and metallization. Semiconductor materials are a meaningful but minority part of the business.

Specialty chemicals maker whose electronics unit supplies wafer bumping, copper interconnect, photomask and packaging chemistries. Semiconductor packaging materials are a meaningful part of the business alongside PCB and industrial chemistry.

Specialty materials maker supplying vapor deposition targets, microelectronics packaging and precious-metal preforms for semiconductor fabs. Semiconductor materials are a meaningful part among several other end markets.

Producer of indium phosphide and gallium arsenide substrates used for lasers, photonics and RF. Wafers are the whole product, but they are compound-semiconductor substrates for optical and RF uses rather than leading-edge logic wafers.
Back-end assembly, bumping and test provider focused on memory, logic and display driver ICs. Packaging services are central, but its work is mostly conventional rather than advanced packaging.

Industrial components maker whose Advanced Surface Technologies unit cleans and coats parts for semiconductor equipment, and whose seals serve fabs. Semiconductor-related work is a meaningful minority of the business.
Software and test-chip provider for semiconductor yield analytics, including assembly and packaging data. It serves foundries and OSATs but is a data and analytics layer, not a supplier of capacity.
